This criminal appeal U/S 374 (2) Cr.P.C. has been filed by the appellant for setting aside the
judgment and order of learned Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Pocso Act), Barabanki
dated 13.09.2023 in Criminal Trial No. 147 of 2017 (State Vs. Prakash) arising out of Case Crime No.
312 of 2017 under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Pocso Act, Police Station Kursi,
District Barabanki convicting the appellant under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 4 of
Pocso Act, and sentencing the appellant under section 363 I.P.C. for five years rigorous
imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000/- and in default of fine six months additional rigorous
imprisonment, under Section 366 Ipc for seven years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000/-
and in default of payment of fine six months additional rigorous imprisonment, under Section 376
Ipc ten years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default of payment of fine six
months additional rigorous imprisonment and under section 4 of Pocso Act, ten years rigorous
imprisonment and fine of Rs. 10,000 and in default of payment of fine six months additional

Order on bail application By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged
on bail during the pendency of the appeal in Criminal Trial No. 147 of 2017 (State Vs. Prakash)
arising out of Case Crime No. 312 of 2017, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of
Pocso Act, Police Station Kursi, District Barabanki.

Shri Shri Santosh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant-appellant contends that the trial court misread the evidences and also neglected to consider material parts of the evidences which vitiate the trial court judgment.

The following arguments in particular made on behalf of appellant could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Nikhil Singh, learned AGA from the record from the record, which entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 15 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2. The learned trial court erred in law by finding the victim to be a minor and applying the POCSO Act to the facts of this case.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant contests the age of the victim set out in the prosecution and points out the failure of the learned trial court to appraise the evidences correctly in accordance with law and in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life. There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victim in the school records.

(ii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 17 years of age respectively.

sentences.text: 2 Two submissions are made in regard to the aforesaid medical report.
Firstly, the range of error in determining the age is about two years and the same should be read in favour of the applicant at this stage.
Secondly, the relevant scientific parameters as per latest medical protocol which would establish the majority of the victim has been excluded from consideration in the medical report.
The medical report is flawed.
In fact the victim is a major.
4. The victim and the applicant were intimate.
5. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.
6. The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
She has asserted that she eloped with the applicant of her own volition to get married to him.
The two resided together in Sitapur and had a consensual physical relationship.

7. No allegation of abduction, wrongful detention or commission of rape has been made by the victim against the applicant in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C.
8.These aspects were never reconciled and with the testimony of the victim and the contradictions in the prosecution case were overlooked by the trial court.
9. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places.
She did not raise an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
Her conduct shows that she was a consenting party.
10. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim was not produced by the prosecution in the trial.
11. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicant with the offence.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
13. The applicant has sanguine hope of succeeding in the appeal in view of the errors committed by the learned trial court while appreciating the evidence.
14. The appeal before this Court is not likely to be heard in any time in the near future.
15. Inordinate delay in hearing of the appeal will led to an indefinite detention of the appellant.
16. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen had always cooperated with the investigation and joined the trial proceedings.
The applicant is not likely to reoffend.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
